вообще-то.gloss: actually, as a matter of fact

meanings.en: actually, as a matter of fact, for the record

examples.text: Меня вообще-то Юля зовут. Вот сахар.
examples.trans: My name is actually Yulia. Here's the sugar.

вставать.gloss: to get up, to stand up

meanings.note: Out of bed or from the floor.

examples.trans: Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
I get up at seven in the morning.
Come on, Tuzik, let's get up!
Viktor Petrovich needs to sleep well.

examples.text: Виктору Петровичу надо хорошо выспаться перед сменой.
examples.trans: Viktor Petrovich needs to get a good night's sleep before the shift.

examples.text: В выходной день я наконец смогу спокойно выспаться.
examples.trans: On my day off I will finally be able to get enough sleep in peace.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
+ dative of person + accusative of thing
imperative давай/давайте + 1st person plural or infinitive

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.
examples.trans: Let's fire him and put you in his place.

related.gloss: to hand in; to take (an exam)

examples.trans: Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

related.gloss: to reach, walk as far as

examples.trans: Cutting a living person with a knife!
You can't torture a living person like that!

examples.text: Нина, ну как ты могла? Живого человека ножом резать!
examples.trans: Nina, how could you? Cutting a living person with a knife!

meanings.note: A door, a shop, or a legal case.

examples.text: А потом, Аркадий Борисович, мы закроем ваше дело.
examples.trans: And then, Arkady Borisovich, we will close your case.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.en: что ли = or what, I suppose

examples.trans: I don't know whether he is at home.

hesitation, at the start of a sentence

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.trans: Can I go and have a look?

пустить.gloss: to let go; to let in

meanings.note: once; что скажешь? = what do you say?

examples.trans: Tell us, when will your programme be out?

сойти.gloss: to get off; (с ума) to go mad

meanings.en: to get off, to step down
сойти с ума = to go mad, to lose one's mind

examples.trans: What, have I lost my mind?

examples.text: Позвонить Третьякову? Я что, с ума сошёл?
examples.trans: Call Tretyakov? What, have I lost my mind?

meanings.en: to ask (a question, or someone: спросить у кого-то)

examples.text: А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Ask him where he put the computer lab.

examples.text: Да? А спросите у него, куда он дел компьютерный класс.
examples.trans: Really? Then ask him where he put the computer lab.

meanings.note: At the start of a question.

examples.trans: So I shouldn't wait for you?
So I shouldn't wait for you tonight?

творить.gloss: to do, to perpetrate; to create

meanings.en: to do, to get up to (something outrageous)
meanings.note: colloquial: что вы творите? = what are you doing?

examples.text: Он сам не понимает, что творит.
examples.trans: He doesn't know what he is doing himself.

examples.text: Самсоновы, вы что творите? Хватит, я прошу вас!
examples.trans: Samsonovs, what are you doing? Stop it, I beg you!

examples.text: Всё, хорошо, я тебя выпущу! Только собаку не трогай!
examples.trans: All right, fine, I'll let you out! Just don't touch the dog!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
